title: The AI Ledger
introduction: The last complete week in AI models and coding harnesses: October 26–November 1, 2026. Coverage focuses on Codex, Claude Code, Copilot and OpenCode, with historical context and a forecast for November 2–8. Older unconfirmed reporting is explicitly marked as a carry-over watch item. Confidence is qualitative, not a calibrated probability. Post-publication update, November 2 at 20:00 UTC: LongCat-2.5 API availability is included below as a dated daily supplement, outside the reporting week. The original weekly archive and November 2–8 forecast are unchanged.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 2: LongCat-2.5 reaches the API
items.summary: LongCat's official API changelog marks LongCat-2.5 available on November 2, following a November 1 announcement. The company positions it for visual understanding and long-running coding tasks, and lists compatibility with Claude Code, Codex and Hermes.
items.whyItMatters: A new model can enter existing coding workflows without a wholly new harness. Compatibility is the vendor's claim, not evidence that every setup works unchanged or that it outperforms alternatives.
items.confidenceReason: Official dated API documentation establishes the availability announcement. Capability and harness-compatibility claims remain vendor-reported and were not independently tested here.
items.historicalContext: The same changelog dates LongCat-2.5-Preview to September 25. The full-model blog is dated November 1; the API availability entry is November 2. This is a preview-to-release progression, not two separate model launches.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra rolls out
items.summary: OpenAI announced Terra for its API, ChatGPT Work and Codex—not Chat. Listed standard API prices are $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens.
items.whyItMatters: Teams have another deployment option; they should test quality on their own workloads instead of treating price as a capability ranking.
items.confidenceReason: Official release documentation establishes the announcement and listed terms, not independent comparative performance.
items.historicalContext: GPT-4o mini's July 2024 launch also emphasized cost-efficient deployment. Different capability classes make raw token-price comparisons misleading.

items.title: Codex CLI 0.165 adds Terra and more session control
items.summary: The October 27 release adds GPT-6.1 Terra to model catalogs, a built-in Google Cloud Vertex AI provider, repository filtering, and in-conversation reasoning-effort changes for supported models.
items.whyItMatters: The harness is changing alongside the model: provider choice and session organization affect how coding work actually runs.
items.confidenceReason: High confidence in the published release announcement; rollout and configuration can vary. No independent productivity gain is claimed.
items.historicalContext: The preceding 0.164 release on October 23 added reusable prompt presets and inline model/permission controls. These are successive workflow changes, not evidence of a benchmark jump.

items.title: Copilot connects coding sessions across surfaces
items.summary: GitHub announced a connected cloud experience on paid Copilot plans. Sessions can continue across web, mobile, CLI, app and VS Code, with cloud sandboxes and shared Actions compute entitlement.
items.whyItMatters: Session continuity and execution environments are becoming central product features. GitHub says sandbox usage billing begins in November; teams should check their entitlement.
items.confidenceReason: High confidence in the published release announcement; rollout and configuration can vary. No independent productivity gain is claimed.
items.historicalContext: GitHub describes this as a connected successor to its separate Copilot Chat and coding-agent experiences. The shift is from isolated surfaces toward resumable work.

items.title: OpenCode 2.2.5 improves compaction and worktree controls
items.summary: The October 30 release adds percentage-based context buffers, worktree/base-branch shortcuts, and fixes for context-window errors and model-switch reasoning handling.
items.whyItMatters: A buffer expressed as a percentage can adapt across model context sizes. These are concrete harness ergonomics and reliability changes, not a new underlying model.
items.confidenceReason: High confidence in the published release announcement; rollout and configuration can vary. No independent productivity gain is claimed.
items.historicalContext: Previously the buffer setting accepted a token count; percentage support makes one configuration more portable across differently sized model windows.

items.title: Claude Code adds subagent effort and budget controls
items.summary: Claude Code 2.1.316 adds a default subagent-effort setting and pooled group budgets in the Claude apps gateway. It also fixes shell processes left running when Claude Code exits itself.
items.whyItMatters: Teams can control delegated work more explicitly. Gateway-specific budget features should not be confused with universal personal-plan controls.
items.confidenceReason: High confidence in the published release announcement; rollout and configuration can vary. No independent productivity gain is claimed.
items.historicalContext: The release changes the previous default of subagents inheriting session effort when no other setting names one. It illustrates increasingly granular agent orchestration.

items.title: Carry-over watch · Oct 19: Anthropic intent-model report
items.summary: The Information reports that Anthropic is preparing a model better at interpreting users' intentions.
items.whyItMatters: Older unconfirmed reporting, carried over for monitoring—not a new development from this issue’s reporting week. No independently verified name, launch date or benchmark is established here.
items.confidenceReason: The original headline is public but the article is paywalled. A dated secondary account attributes the report to one unnamed user; repetition does not create independent corroboration.
items.historicalContext: Recent announced model releases show ongoing iteration, but launch cadence cannot validate this particular rumor or predict its timing.

items.title: Next week: another control upgrade in a coding harness
items.summary: Editorial forecast for November 2–8: at least one of Codex, Copilot, OpenCode or Claude Code will announce a new session, context-management, or subagent-control feature.
items.whyItMatters: Model capability alone is not the whole developer experience. Worktree continuity, context management and delegated-work controls are actionable dimensions to evaluate.
items.confidenceReason: The last complete week contains relevant releases from all four projects. That supports a modest directional forecast, but provides neither a calibrated probability nor a promised roadmap.
items.historicalContext: October brought Codex session filtering, Copilot cloud continuity, OpenCode context-buffer controls, and Claude Code subagent-effort settings. The forecast extrapolates this observed cluster without assuming every vendor follows it.

charts.selectionCriteria: Three billing categories for one model. This is a cost breakdown, not a model ranking or total task-cost estimate.
